summary: Multilingual LLM-based text-to-speech that can match a voice from a short sample, with streaming output and instruction control.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: CosyVoice is a family of text-to-speech models built on large language models, with code for inference, training and deployment. The latest, Fun-CosyVoice 3.0, targets zero-shot multilingual speech in 9 languages (Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Russian) plus 18+ Chinese dialects and accents. It supports streaming both text in and audio out with latency as low as 150 ms per the README, pronunciation fixes with Pinyin or phonemes, and instructions for language, dialect, emotion, speed and volume.
sixtySeconds.problem: Natural, controllable speech in many languages usually needs expensive services. CosyVoice provides open models you can run and deploy yourself.
whoFor: Teams deploying their own TTS service
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Pick it for multilingual, low-latency TTS with dialect support and deployment options like vLLM, Docker and TensorRT-LLM.
requirements: sox (install if you hit compatibility issues)

overview: Clone with submodules, create a Python 3.10 Conda environment and install requirements.txt.
Download pretrained models such as Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B from ModelScope or Hugging Face into pretrained_models/.
Run python example.py to try each model, or start the web demo. Apache-2.0 licensed.

features.title: Zero-shot voices
features.body: Speak in a voice from a sample.

features.title: Bi-streaming
features.body: Text-in and audio-out streaming, about 150 ms latency.

limitations: Setup has many steps and large model downloads
Some optional parts are Linux x86-64 only

install.verificationNote: Commands come from CosyVoice's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

steps.title: Clone with submodules
steps.body: If submodules fail to download, run git submodule update --init --recursive inside the folder until it succeeds.

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.code:
conda create -n cosyvoice -y python=3.10
conda activate cosyvoice

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.body: The README's command adds an Aliyun mirror; plain pip install -r requirements.txt works outside China.

steps.title: Download a model
steps.body: In Python: from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download; snapshot_download('FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512', local_dir='pretrained_models/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B'). ModelScope works too.

steps.title: Run a server
steps.body: The README shows docker run commands for gRPC or FastAPI servers on port 50000 with the NVIDIA runtime.

firstRun.title: Run example.py
firstRun.body: Generate speech with each downloaded model.

tutorial.title: Try CosyVoice in the web demo

steps.title: Switch models
steps.body: Use CosyVoice-300M-SFT or CosyVoice-300M-Instruct for those inference modes.

tutorial.expected: Speech generated from your text in the browser.

costs.label: CosyVoice
costs.value: Free and open source under Apache-2.0.

troubleshooting.solution: Install sox and libsox-dev (Ubuntu) or sox and sox-devel (CentOS).
Use vLLM 0.9.0 or 0.11.x+ in a separate cloned environment; other versions are unsupported or untested.
Run git submodule update --init --recursive until it succeeds.
